newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish textile producer Bisas to float shares.
newsitem.headline: Turkish textile producer Bisas to float shares.

text.p: Turkish cotton fabric producer Bisas Tekstil Sanayi ve Ticaret will offer 42 billion lira worth of new shares to the public at a fixed price of 5,200 lira per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share on Thursday and Friday.
Consortium leader Korfezbank said Bisas would waive 42 billion lira of preemptive rights to sell them to the public when raising its capital to 208 billion lira from 52 billion.
It said 40 percent of the total offer would be allocated to foreign investors and 10 percent to domestic institutional investors. Brokerage house Ekinciler Yatirim ve Menkul will co-manage the offer.
The company will have floated 20.2 percent of its capital if all of the offer is sold.
Bisas which produces cotton, polyester, acrylic, flax and mixed fabrics, is owned 90.5 percent by Bisas Bursa Iplik Sanayii, one of Turkey's three leading fibre producers, the bank said.

Bisas Tekstil posted 114.1 billion lira of net profits in 1995 and 32 billion lira in the first half of 1996. Its net sales were 932.3 billion lira last year and 643.4 billion in the first half. 1996 sales are predicted to reach 1.6 trillion lira.
The company's fabric production capacity increased to about 14-15 million metres per year in September from previous 7.5 million metres after the completion of machinery investments.
